# Colour options

The colours of the points can be changed. The default is Paul Tol's bright
palette (`"tol_bright"`) but you can select from:

- `"tol_bright"`
- `"tol_vibrant"`
- `"tol_muted"`
- `"tol_light"`
- `"tol_rainbow"`
- or Color Universal Design (`"cud"`)

```{r colours}
library(SuperPlotR)
superplot(lord_jcb, "Speed", "Treatment", "Replicate",
          ylab = "Speed (µm/min)", pal = "cud")
```

If you have more than 8-10 conditions, the `"tol_rainbow"` palette is a good
choice as it has 27 colours. The other palettes have fewer colours and will
repeat if you have more conditions than colours.

If you like the palette, but don't like the order of the colours, you can change
the order with the `pal_order` argument. For example, to reverse the order of
the colours:

```{r pal_order}
superplot(lord_jcb, "Speed", "Treatment", "Replicate",
          ylab = "Speed (µm/min)", pal = "tol_bright", pal_order = "reverse")
```

or you can randomise the order of the colours:

```{r pal_order_random}
superplot(lord_jcb, "Speed", "Treatment", "Replicate",
          ylab = "Speed (µm/min)", pal = "tol_bright", pal_order = "random")
```

or you can specify a custom order of the colours by providing a vector of
integers corresponding to the order of the conditions.
Using "random" will print an order of integers that you can use in the next
SuperPlot() call to reproduce the colours, since the next time you call with
"random", it will be different!

Note that previous versions of SuperPlotR used `tol_bright` in the following
orders (for 1 to 6 replicates:
`list(c(1), c(1, 2), c(1, 4, 2), c(1, 3, 4, 2), c(1, 5, 3, 4, 2), c(1, 5, 3, 4, 2, 6))`

It's also possible to supply your own palette as a vector of colours (in hex or
description format)

```{r custom_palette}
superplot(lord_jcb, "Speed", "Treatment", "Replicate",
          ylab = "Speed (µm/min)", pal = c("#ff3faf", "blue", "grey"))
```
